1.say: Check that. The heart pumps blood. Does it make blood or oxygen?
hit: The heart makes blood and pumps it around the body to bring oxygen.
the circulatory system creates oxygen for the cells
miss: The circulatory system transports oxygen, nutrients, and other substances throughout the body, and it removes wastes from the tissues.
The heart pumps blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to the cells and takes away wastes.
The heart does not make blood, it pumps it.

5.say: Check that. The myocardium is the heart wall's thick muscle layer. Is it a covering or a chamber?
hit: The myocardium is a layer that covers the heart.
The myocardium is a chamber of the heart.
miss: The myocardium is the thick layer of cardiac muscle that makes up most of the heart wall.
The myocardium is thick cardiac muscle in the heart wall.
Myocardium is the heart muscle that pumps blood.

6.say: Check that. Keeping the blood from mixing is the septum's job. What does a valve do?
hit: A valve keeps oxygen rich and oxygen poor blood from mixing.
valves stop the blood from mixing
miss: A valve is a flap that keeps blood flowing in only one direction, so it cannot flow backward.
A valve is a flap so blood only goes one way. The septum keeps blood from mixing.
Valves keep blood from flowing backward.

7.say: Check that. Where does blood pick up oxygen, in the heart or in the lungs?
hit: Blood picks up oxygen in the heart.
the blood gets oxygen from the heart and goes to the lungs
miss: Pulmonary circulation carries blood between the heart and the lungs. The right side of the heart pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.
Blood goes from the heart to the lungs to pick up oxygen and then back to the heart.
The right side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs where it gets oxygen.

8.say: Check that. In the body, does blood pick up oxygen or drop it off?
hit: In systemic circulation the blood picks up oxygen from the body.
blood gets oxygen in the tissues and goes back to the heart
miss: Systemic circulation carries blood between the heart and the rest of the body. The left side of the heart pumps oxygen-rich blood to the body.
The left side pumps oxygen rich blood to the body, where the cells get oxygen from the blood.
Blood drops off oxygen at the body and picks up carbon dioxide.

9.say: Check that. Is the blood in the pulmonary arteries oxygen rich or oxygen poor?
hit: The pulmonary arteries carry oxygen rich blood to the lungs.
the pulmonary artery takes oxygen rich blood
miss: The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary arteries to the lungs. Oxygen-rich blood comes back through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium.
Pulmonary arteries carry oxygen poor blood to the lungs, and pulmonary veins bring oxygen rich blood back.

9.say: Check that. Which chamber pumps blood to the lungs, an atrium or a ventricle?
hit: The right atrium pumps blood to the lungs.
the right atrium sends blood into the lungs
miss: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs.
Blood enters the right atrium, then the right ventricle pumps it to the lungs.
Blood from the lungs comes back to the left atrium.

10.say: Check that. The aorta leaves the left ventricle. Is that blood oxygen rich or oxygen poor?
hit: The aorta carries oxygen poor blood to the body.
the aorta has oxygen poor blood
miss: The left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aorta to the body. Oxygen-poor blood comes back through veins into the right atrium.
The aorta carries oxygen rich blood to the body.
Oxygen poor blood returns to the right atrium, not the aorta.

12.say: Check that. Which vessels have valves, arteries or veins?
hit: Arteries have valves to keep blood moving away from the heart.
arteries use one way valves
miss: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Their walls are thick and elastic so they can withstand the high pressure of blood pumped by the heart.
Arteries do not have valves like veins do.
Arteries have thick elastic walls for high pressure, and veins have valves.

13.say: Check that. Which way do oxygen and wastes move between the blood and the cells?
hit: Oxygen moves from the cells into the blood through the thin walls.
wastes go from the blood into the cells
miss: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels. Their walls are one cell thick so oxygen, nutrients, and wastes can pass easily between the blood and the body's cells.
Oxygen and nutrients move from the blood into the cells, and wastes move from the cells into the blood.
Capillaries are tiny so oxygen can pass from the blood to the cells.

14.re: \bveins? (have no|has no|don't have|dont have|do not have|does not have|doesn't have|doesnt have|lack|lacks) valves?\b
14.say: Check that. What inside veins keeps blood from flowing backward?
hit: Veins have no valves, so muscles push the blood back to the heart.
veins do not have valves
miss: Veins carry blood back toward the heart. Valves keep the blood from flowing backward, and skeletal muscles squeeze the veins to push blood along.
Veins have valves that stop blood from flowing backward.
Arteries have no valves but veins do.
